# codebase-superman

"Superman" multi-agent experiment. Archive.

## Stack & contents

Next.js / TypeScript with a built-in MCP server (`codevault-mcp`). ~205 files under `code/superman/{app,codevault-mcp,docs/superpowers}`. MCP tools: analyze / apply / ask / gaps / simulate / validate. Includes `.codevault-memory.json` and a production retrieval-pipeline spec dated 2026-03-25.

## Why this is here

Most concrete prior art for an EMA-side **code-intelligence MCP**. The retrieval-pipeline-design spec is direct input if/when EMA exposes a code-intelligence vApp.

## How to load it efficiently

```bash
git show origin/codebase-superman:code/superman/codevault-mcp/index.ts
git show origin/codebase-superman:code/superman/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-25-retrieval-pipeline-design.md
```

## Doctrine extracted (2026-04-22)

Carries forward (principles, not code):
- **Staged retrieval** — decompose → parallel candidate generation → graph expansion → multi-signal rerank → budgeted assembly. Each stage swappable, no single-pass keyword retrieval (`code/superman/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-25-retrieval-pipeline-design.md`).
- **No silent tool failures** — every error returns a next-step instruction (`call check_status, then analyze_repo`) so the calling agent can self-recover (`codevault-mcp/index.ts` `formatError` and `check_status.nextStep`).
- **First-class status probe** — health/status reports `active | stale | initializing` plus an auto-recovery hint, and is the first contract any agent surface exposes (`codevault-mcp/index.ts` `check_status` tool definition).

Leaves behind (residue):
- The specific OpenAI embedding + Qdrant + `.codevault-cache.json` wiring and 50K context budget.
- The MCP/Zod TypeScript surface and the per-node intent-graph dump in `.codevault-memory.json`.

Topic relevance: `memory`, `recovery`, `orchestration`, `driver`, `doctrine`.
